'''Christopher Jarzynski''' is an American physicist and distinguished university professor at [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]'s department of chemistry and biochemistry, department of physics, and institute for physical science and technology, and fellow of the National Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.umd.edu/faculty-staff-directory/facultydirectory/christopher-jarzynski|title=Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry – University of Maryland, College Park MD Christopher Jarzynski - Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-14}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/features/4266|title=UMD's Christopher Jarzynski Awarded American Physical Society's Lars Onsager Prize|last=Ying|first=Irene|date=2018-11-06|website=College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814012553/https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/features/4266|archive-date=2019-08-14|access-date=2019-08-14|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=UMD's Christopher Jarzynski Elected to the National Academy of Sciences|url=https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/features/4575|last=abbyr|date=2020-04-27|website=College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences|language=en|access-date=2020-04-30|archive-date=2020-06-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616223139/https://cmns.umd.edu/news-events/features/4575|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is known for his contributions to [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics]] and [[statistical mechanics]], for which he was awarded the 2019 [[Lars Onsager Prize]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=2018 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2019-08-14}}</ref> In 1997, he derived the now famous [[Jarzynski equality]], confirmation of which was cited by the Nobel Committee for Physics as an application of one of the winning inventions of the 2018 [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prize in physics]]—[[optical tweezers]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2018/advanced-information/|title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 2018|website=NobelPrize.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-14}}</ref>

==Education and research==
Jarzynski graduated from Our Lady of Good Counsel High School in Wheaton, Maryland in 1983.  He then attended Princeton University from where he graduated with high honors with an A.B. in physics in 1987 after completing a senior thesis titled "An experimental search for 1.7 MEV [[axion]]s in nuclear decays, 'the detector from hell'."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Jarzynski|first=Christopher|url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/4122325|title=An experimental search for 1.7 MEV axions in nuclear decays "the detector from hell"|date=1987|publisher=Princeton, NJ: Department of Physics|language=English}}</ref>  He received his Ph.D. in physics in 1994 from [[University of California, Berkeley]], under the supervision of [[Władysław Świątecki (physicist)|Władysław J. Świątecki]] and [[Robert Grayson Littlejohn]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/images/CV/Jarzynski_CV19.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|last=Jarzynski|first=Christopher|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-08-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=101377|title=Christopher Jarzynski - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-08-14}}</ref>

At University of California, Berkeley, Jarzynski studied adiabatic invariants in chaotic classical systems. After graduating with a PhD, he spent ten years at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], and since 2006 he has been faculty at the University of Maryland, College Park. His research is primarily in the area of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, where he has contributed to an understanding of how the laws of thermodynamics apply to nanoscale systems. In 1997, he derived an equality, now known as the [[Jarzynski equality]], that relates nonequilibrium fluctuations to equilibrium free energy differences, a result that has been verified in numerous experiments and has found applications in biophysics and [[computational chemistry]]. His current interests also include the thermodynamics of information processing, as well as shortcuts to adiabaticity in quantum, classical and stochastic systems.

== Awards and honours ==
He has been the recipient of a [[Fulbright Fellowship]], the [[Sackler Prize]] in the Physical Sciences, and the 2019 [[Lars Onsager Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Lars Onsager Prize recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Jarzynski&first_nm=Christopher&year=2019 |access-date=2020-04-24 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In 2020 he was elected to the [[Member of the National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] and awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] and [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellowship]].<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Christopher Jarzynski|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/christopher-jarzynski/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2020/02/21/2020-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/|date=2020-02-21|website=Simons Foundation|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-30}}</ref>

Jarzynski is a member of the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment]]'', and an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of Statistical Physics]]''.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />
